scope: Native motion-worker synchronous BDX event path and STATUS observer concurrency; no claim that a retail motion event uses the General status setter
decision: A sole game-thread STATUS notification contract is insufficient for the observed native call graph. The ledger now admits serialized notifications from multiple native threads with per-thread nesting; no native hook or timed STATUS transaction is installed.

conditions: Worker jobs enabled and actor left for the batched path; actors with Actor+2496 are handled synchronously first.
Model/motion data exposes a newly present flagged motion event.
Actor+1456 points to a BDX context with event27.
threading.statusLimit: A BDX event can reach native traps, including the registered3C2650 adapter, but no retail event27 bytecode using that trap has been identified here.
threading.globalLimit: 3E1840/3E1C80 explicitly save/set process-wide current-VM globals. This evidence does not establish how all shipped actors avoid concurrent VM execution; do not claim those globals are thread-local or protected by an unseen lock.

properties: 80 bounded STATUS slots; pool epoch, allocation token, five field revisions, nonwrapping process-local serial.
Before-entry invalidation including same-value writes; disjoint field masks remain independent.
32 outstanding frames with per-thread LIFO, arbitrary cross-thread exit order and no allocation/compare while any writer remains active.
Native abnormal exit faults the ledger, so a failed release/reset is never misreported as known deallocation.
Bootstrap adoption requires a separately validated live allocation. A retired slot requires an observed Initialize before capture.
Notifications require caller serialization; release that lock before the native original. The pure model itself contains no synchronization or installed hooks.

tests.scope: Isolated metadata state machine. No claim of installed callback, IPC receipt or gameplay verification.
